## About the Book
Man Amongst the Clouds is a literary fantasy novel where magic is memory. Every stone remembers the mountain it was part of. Every flame remembers the first spark. In this world, a boy named Aelo is raised on silence by a guardian named Jalo, whose every lie is an act of love. They are hunted by The Knife, an assassin who carries a wooden box of five beautiful objects as the only proof he was ever a person. He was sent by King Varas — a ruler born deaf to the Song in a world where everything sings, who has spent seventy years draining others' memories to fill his silence.

The magic system features seven disciplines, each a different way of hearing the world's memory, and each exacting an irreversible personal cost:
1. The Know — empathic communion with every living thing. Cost: your emotional boundaries.
2. The Mold — reshaping matter through its memory. Cost: the feeling in your hands.
3. The Heal — reminding flesh of wholeness. Cost: you carry every wound you mend.
4. The Move — folding distance through spatial memory. Cost: your sense of where you are.
5. The Guide — reading the memory of paths and journeys. Cost: your memory of home.
6. The Burn — awakening fire from the world's first memory. Cost: the warmth inside you.
7. The Sing — harmonizing all seven voices at once. The rarest discipline. Cost: everything — you dissolve into the memory of the world itself.

The novel is structured in five parts:
- Part I: The Still Water
- Part II: The Waking
- Part III: The Burning
- Part IV: The Song
- Part V: The Morning

The complete novel spans 48 chapters with a prologue and epilogue.

## Comparable Authors
Man Amongst the Clouds is for readers who love:
- Patrick Rothfuss (The Name of the Wind, Kingkiller Chronicle) — lyrical prose, deeply personal magic system
- Robin Hobb (Assassin's Apprentice, Farseer Trilogy) — devastating mentor-student relationships, deep interiority
- Guy Gavriel Kay (Tigana) — memory as theme, literary gravity, a villain rooted in grief
- Ursula K. Le Guin (A Wizard of Earthsea) — magic as discipline and balance, coming of age

## About the Author
Justin Cronk is an American author and military veteran. He is the author of Man Amongst the Clouds, a 146,000-word literary fantasy novel published by Stillfire Press in March 2026. He co-founded Stillfire Press with his son Carter Cronk, who is writing the dark fantasy novel Ash to Fury (coming 2027). Cronk spent nine years writing Man Amongst the Clouds, developing a magic system based on memory drawn from Traditional Chinese Medicine, alchemical spagyrics, and herbalism. His life experiences — military service in Iraq, uranium exploration in Colorado and Utah, and work at a remote camp in Nunavut, Canada — directly informed the novel's world-building.

## About Stillfire Press
Stillfire Press is an independent fantasy publishing house founded by father-son duo Justin Cronk and Carter Cronk. Every manuscript is blockchain-verified on the Polygon network. Readers can buy direct from the authors — 97% of every sale goes to the writer. Their two debut novels are Man Amongst the Clouds (literary fantasy, 2026) and Ash to Fury (dark fantasy, 2027).

## Key Characters
- Aelo — The protagonist. A boy raised on silence who discovers he can hear the world sing. He possesses the rarest discipline: The Sing.
- Jalo — Aelo's guardian. A man whose every lie is an act of love. He raised Aelo in hiding for fifteen years.
- The Knife — An assassin who carries a wooden box of five beautiful objects as the only proof he was ever a person. Sent by King Varas to find Aelo.
- King Varas — The antagonist. Born deaf to the Song in a world where everything sings. He has spent seventy years draining others' memories to fill his silence.
- Laine — A healer who carries every wound she mends.
- Sereth — A Guide who always knows the way forward but can never remember the way back.

## Amazon Reviews
"I picked up Man Amongst the Clouds not really knowing what to expect, and it ended up sticking with me more than most books I've read lately. This isn't a fast, plot-driven story — it's more reflective and philosophical, but in a way that feels intentional rather than slow. The writing has a kind of raw honesty to it, like the author is working through something real instead of just telling a story." — Verified Amazon Purchase, 5 stars

"It's not your typical fantasy, which is what makes it so good. It's more thoughtful and character-driven, and the writing just feels real. There were a few moments that really stuck with me even after I finished." — Verified Amazon Purchase, 5 stars
